What to look for in textile trousers

  • Match your jacket. A 360° connection zip keeps your suit together in a crash — stick to one brand range where you can.
  • Knee and hip armour. CE Level 2 at the knees is the minimum; hip protectors matter in low-speed falls too.
  • Boot gaiters. Internal gaiters seal over your boots and stop rain running into your footwear.
  • Riding-position fit. Always try trousers seated — check the waist, knee articulation and length in your riding posture.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on textile trousers?

Our catalogue spans £107.99 to £1,000. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Klim, RST, Merlin, Spada. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Textile or leather?

Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport touring. Many riders own both.

faq.q: Why choose textile trousers over riding jeans?
faq.a: Textile trousers offer more protection, better waterproofing and greater versatility than jeans, making them the go-to for touring and all-weather riding. They typically include laminated waterproof membranes, CE knee and hip armour, ventilation and adjustable fit. Jeans win on everyday casual style, but for long distances in changeable UK weather, textile trousers keep you drier, warmer and better protected.

faq.q: Should I match my trousers to my jacket?
faq.a: Ideally yes. A jacket-to-trouser connection zip clips the two together so they cannot separate and ride up in a slide, keeping your lower back covered. Buying trousers and jacket from the same brand and range guarantees the zips are compatible. RST and Klim both design their kit to connect, so pairing pieces from one range is the safest approach.

The better options use a laminated membrane such as Gore-Tex (Klim) or a bonded waterproof laminate (RST Pro Series), which keeps you dry in sustained rain without a separate liner. Cheaper trousers may use a removable inner membrane that works but is slower to deploy. Look for taped seams and, over time, refresh the outer DWR coating to keep water beading off.

faq.q: What armour do textile trousers need?
faq.a: Look for CE-certified knee armour as a minimum, ideally with adjustable positioning so it sits over your knee in a riding position. Hip protectors are equally important and are included on better trousers such as the RST Pro Series with D3O armour, though some have empty pockets for optional inserts. Fitting CE hip armour where possible is a worthwhile upgrade.

faq.q: Can I wear textile trousers in summer?
faq.a: Yes, if you choose a design with good ventilation. Vented options like the Klim XC Lite V6 flow air on warm days, and many laminated trousers have zipped vents to dump heat. Fully sealed winter-focused trousers can run hot in summer, so consider a lighter or more heavily vented pair if most of your riding is in warm weather.
